reader.requirement: At --std 85 an indexed file's file description entry must begin with the level indicator FD, written before file-name-1; an entry with no FD, with file-name-1 before FD, or with FD and no file-name is refused, and an indexed file described by SD instead is refused.

edition-consulted.switches: whether FD is a reserved word at each edition: true at 85, 2002, 2014 and 2023

reader.edition-search: The grammar rule `FD fileName fileDescriptionClauses? DOT dataDescriptionEntry*` has no semantic predicate; grepped src for FileDescriptionEntryContext/VisitFileDescriptionEntry (only the generated parser, ClosedFormats, AreaPlacementPass, LevelNumberPass, OoDefinitionRules: none switches on edition for the FD-before-file-name order).
reader.witnesses-cover: part: pb1238 exercises admitted FD formats (legal side); the refusal forms (no FD, reversed order, FD without file-name, SD for an indexed file) are probed here.

probes.printed: COBOL1900 x3 (§1985:XI.2.3.3 SR2: only ASSIGN may follow a sort file's file-name) and COBOL1692 on OPEN/CLOSE
probes.expected: refused: an indexed file is described by FD, not SD
FD on its own line, file-name on the next, with the 1985 BLOCK/LABEL/RECORD/VALUE OF/DATA RECORDS clauses, compiles and runs

citations.check: OK  §1985:IX.3.2.3 SR1  (3.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1

reader.notes: The order is fixed by the grammar production itself, the same at every edition; FD is reserved in all four editions. The parse refusal COBOL0001 is terse but names the offending token at its position.

refuter.evidence: r6comment: FD, a comment line, then IX on its own line with LABEL RECORDS -> compiles and runs (RAN, exit 0), the order FD then file-name-1 kept across lines; r6ws: an FD entry written in WORKING-STORAGE -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'FD' (the level indicator is recognized only where a file description entry may begin). The grammar production fixes the order at every edition, so there is no edition arm to miss. cite.py: OK  §1985:IX.3.2.3 SR1  (3.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1.
